name: Calderwick
basis: Original setting written for Prospero Dungeon.
summary: A smoky river and canal town in the Pennine foothills that made its fortune drawing metal tube and building pneumatic dispatch systems: the cash carriers in shop ceilings, the message tubes in banks and the town's own pneumatic post.

curated-2026-10.title: Calderwick, an original setting written for Prospero Dungeon
curated-2026-10.note: Invented town with no real counterpart. Its texture follows ordinary late-Victorian life in the textile and engineering towns of the West Riding and Lancashire: canal basins, workers' terraces, temperance halls, mechanics' institutes, wakes weeks, Whit walks and municipal parks. Rents are weekly, in shillings, for one room, two rooms and a small whole house. Climate is rounded from Pennine-town normals with winter smog added for the setting.

neighborhoods.name: Castle Hill
neighborhoods.summary: The old town on the hill: the ruined castle, the parish church, crooked stone lanes and the tall houses of the families who owned the land before the works came.

neighborhoods.name: Lowfield
neighborhoods.summary: The works district on the flat river land: tube mills, foundries and pump shops, chimneys in every direction and a hooter at six each morning.

neighborhoods.name: Saltergate Basin
neighborhoods.summary: The canal basin where the Calder and Aske Navigation meets the river: warehouses, wharf cranes, horse-boat stables and boat families living aboard.

neighborhoods.name: Hobcroft
neighborhoods.summary: Rows of red-brick workers' terraces up the slope from Lowfield, with corner shops, a wash-house, chapels and washing strung across the back streets on Mondays.

neighborhoods.name: Ings End
neighborhoods.summary: Newer through-terraces on the old water meadows downstream, built by the Co-operative building society, with allotments running down to the river.

neighborhoods.name: Exchange Quarter
neighborhoods.summary: The respectable merchant quarter: banks, insurance offices, the Exchange, the department store and the town's first pneumatic post office.

neighborhoods.name: Station Fields
neighborhoods.summary: The railway quarter around Calderwick Central: goods yards, the engine shed, commercial hotels, cab ranks and the music hall.

neighborhoods.name: Market Place
neighborhoods.summary: The market district below Castle Hill: the covered market hall, Saturday stalls on the setts, tripe shops, pawnbrokers and the Theatre Royal.

neighborhoods.name: Paradise
neighborhoods.summary: The immigrant quarter around Paradise Street, settled by Irish labourers who dug the canal and later by Italian families: ice-cream carts, a Catholic church and crowded courts.

neighborhoods.name: Ackroyd Park
neighborhoods.summary: Villas and better terraces around the park that Hannah Ackroyd, widow of a tube-mill owner, gave the town, with its glasshouse, lake and bandstand.

neighborhoods.name: Moorside
neighborhoods.summary: The institute district on the road up to the moor: the Pennock Institute, the art school, the infirmary, the museum and lodgings full of students and nurses.

neighborhoods.name: Fernleigh
neighborhoods.summary: Where the new money lives: big stone villas of the tube and pump manufacturers, each with a carriage drive, a conservatory and a message tube to the works.

neighborhoods.name: Ridley Moor
neighborhoods.summary: Open moor above the town with reservoirs, a few farms and the airship mooring mast where the mail ship ties up.

neighborhoods.name: Calder Holme
neighborhoods.summary: The riverside pleasure ground upstream of the works, with the lido, the velodrome, a pier on the old mill dam and Sunday crowds in summer.

transit.name: Kirkgate steam tram
transit.summary: A small steam tram engine pulling double-deck cars from Station Fields up Kirkgate past the market to Moorside and the park gates.

transit.name: River Road horse tram
transit.summary: Horse trams along the valley bottom from Calder Holme through Lowfield and the basin to Ings End, packed at shift change.

transit.name: Corporation horse omnibuses
transit.summary: Horse buses on the hill routes the trams cannot climb, out to Fernleigh and up to Ridley Moor.

transit.name: Calder Valley local trains
transit.summary: Stopping trains from Calderwick Central down the valley to the neighbouring mill towns and the main line.

transit.name: Canal packet boat
transit.summary: A slow horse-drawn passenger boat on the canal between Saltergate Basin and Calder Holme, popular on summer Sundays.

transit.name: Ridley Moor air mail
transit.summary: One mail airship that flies the bags to the coast and back twice a week, carrying a handful of paying passengers.

transit.name: Hackney cabs
transit.summary: Horse cabs from the station rank and the Exchange, for anyone who can afford a shilling.

places.name: The Old Bell
places.summary: The oldest pub in town, low-beamed, by the church gate; bell-ringers drink there after practice night.

places.name: Calderwick Castle ruins
places.summary: A broken keep and curtain wall on top of the hill with a view over the chimneys and the canal.

places.name: St Wilfrid's parish church
places.summary: The old parish church, blackened by soot, with Sunday services and a Thursday organ recital.

places.name: The Moulders' Arms
places.summary: A works pub at the gates of Dunmore Brothers that opens early for men coming off the night turn.

places.name: Lowfield Amateur Boxing Club
places.summary: A boxing gym in an old pattern shop, with skipping ropes, a ring and Friday night bouts.

places.name: Saltergate wharves
places.summary: The canal wharves where narrowboats unload coal and pig iron and load crated tube for the coast.

places.name: The Navigation Inn
places.summary: A boatmen's pub on the basin with a stable yard behind and a fire in the back room.

places.name: Basin Coffee Tavern
places.summary: A temperance coffee tavern for boat families: mugs of cocoa, bacon breadcakes and newspapers on a rail.

places.name: Hobcroft Public Baths and Wash-house
places.summary: Corporation baths with a swimming bath, slipper baths by the half hour and a steam laundry for washing day.

places.name: Garside's Fish Saloon
places.summary: A fish and chip shop with a back room of oilcloth tables, open till the last pub closes.

places.name: Hope Street Temperance Hall
places.summary: A temperance hall with magic-lantern shows, penny readings, choir practice and a tea urn that never goes cold.

places.name: Ings End allotments
places.summary: Allotment strips down to the river, with leeks, rhubarb, pigeon lofts and sheds for a quiet pipe.

places.name: The Rose and Crown
places.summary: A neighbourhood pub with a bowling green, a darts board and a Saturday sing-song round the piano.

places.name: The Calderwick Exchange
places.summary: The columned Exchange where tube orders and metal prices are dealt on Tuesdays, with a public gallery.

places.name: Bulmer's Chophouse
places.summary: A panelled chophouse for clerks and merchants: chops, steak pudding and stout at long tables.

places.name: Lister's Coffee Rooms
places.summary: Upstairs coffee rooms with chess tables, the London papers and a pneumatic tube to send notes to the Exchange.

places.name: Wright and Battersby
places.summary: The department store, with cash carriers whizzing through ceiling tubes to the counting house and a tea room upstairs.

places.name: Calderwick Free Library
places.summary: The free lending library and newsroom, warm in winter, with a ladies' reading room and a long waiting list for new novels.

places.name: The Railway Tavern
places.summary: A busy pub opposite the station full of porters, commercial travellers and drivers off the late train.

places.name: Thornber's Varieties
places.summary: The music hall: comic singers, a juggler, a ventriloquist and the chorus, twice nightly, with a bar at the back.

places.name: Central Station refreshment room
places.summary: Tea, pork pies and hot soup on the platform, open for the first and last trains.

places.name: Calderwick Market Hall
places.summary: A cast-iron covered market of butchers, cheese stalls, a sweet stall, a herbalist and a mushy-pea stand.

places.name: Saturday open market
places.summary: Stalls on the setts every Saturday selling cloth, crockery, second-hand books and quack remedies, lit by naphtha flares after dark.

places.name: Brierley's Tripe and Cow-heel Shop
places.summary: A tripe dresser's with a dining room behind: tripe and onions, pies and peas, very cheap.

places.name: Whiteley's Cafe
places.summary: A tea room above the confectioner's, with fat rascals, curd tarts and a trio playing on Saturday afternoons.

places.name: Theatre Royal
places.summary: The proper theatre, with touring companies, melodrama, Shakespeare in winter and the pantomime from Boxing Day.

places.name: Rossi's ice-cream parlour
places.summary: An Italian family's parlour that sells ice cream, hot chestnuts in winter and strong coffee all year.

places.name: St Patrick's Hall
places.summary: The Catholic parish hall: Irish dances on Saturday night, whist drives and a boxing tournament at Easter.

places.name: Bonetti's bakery
places.summary: A bakery on Paradise Street selling bread rolls, biscotti and hot pies to the works crowds before six.

places.name: Ackroyd Park
places.summary: The philanthropist's park, with a boating lake, a bandstand, bowling greens and a drinking fountain carved with her motto.

places.name: Ackroyd Palm House
places.summary: The botanic glasshouse in the park, warm and wet, with palms, ferns and a banana plant that fruited once.

places.name: Fernleigh Lawn Tennis Club
places.summary: Grass courts and a pavilion where manufacturers' sons and daughters play doubles and flirt.

places.name: Fernleigh Assembly Rooms
places.summary: Subscription balls, charity bazaars and lectures by visiting explorers.

places.name: Calderwick Museum of Pneumatics
places.summary: The town's own industry museum: the first cash carrier, cutaway compressors and a working tube you can send a message through.

places.name: Calderwick Art Gallery and Museum
places.summary: Paintings given by mill owners, stuffed birds, Roman coins from the castle and a mummy nobody can explain.

places.name: Mechanics' Library
places.summary: The Pennock Institute's lending library of engineering books and trade journals, open to members until nine.

places.name: Moorside Coffee Room
places.summary: A cheap coffee room where students argue over drawings and nurses come off the morning shift.

places.name: Ridley Moor mooring mast
places.summary: The iron mast where the mail airship ties up; people walk up on Tuesdays and Fridays to watch her come in.

places.name: Ridley reservoirs walk
places.summary: A path round the reservoirs and over the moor, above the smoke, with curlews in spring.

places.name: The Moor Cock Inn
places.summary: A stone inn on the moor road serving ham and eggs to walkers and the airship crew.

places.name: Calder Holme Lido
places.summary: An open-air bathing pool fed from the river, cold even in August, with a sand bank and changing huts.

places.name: Calderwick Velodrome
places.summary: A cinder and timber cycle track with Saturday races, betting under the stand and a club for lady cyclists.

places.name: Holme pleasure pier
places.summary: A short pier on the old mill dam with rowing boats, a penny-in-the-slot machine hall and a whelk stall.

places.name: Miss Pickles' tea room
places.summary: A front-room tea room in a stone house below the castle, with seed cake, potted-meat sandwiches and a view of the chimneys.

places.name: Castle Hill bowling green
places.summary: A level green inside the old outer bailey where retired mill managers play crown bowls on summer evenings.

places.name: Lowfield Dining Rooms
places.summary: A works cookshop by the tube mill gates selling hot dinners in basins: meat and potato pie, peas and a mug of tea for fourpence.

places.name: Lowfield Co-operative Store
places.summary: The Co-op grocery and drapery, where members collect their dividend twice a year and argue about it at the counter.

places.name: Ogden's clogger
places.summary: A clogger's shop where wooden soles are cut, irons nailed on and old clogs re-ironed while you wait on the bench.

places.name: Hirst's dry dock
places.summary: A boatyard at the end of the basin where narrowboats are caulked, tarred and painted with roses and castles.

places.name: Boatmen's Mission
places.summary: A small mission chapel on the wharf with a Sunday service, a reading room and a night school for boat children.

places.name: Zion Primitive Methodist Chapel
places.summary: A plain brick chapel with a big Sunday school, a brass band and the anniversary sing on the second Sunday in June.

places.name: Hobcroft recreation ground
places.summary: A cinder field with swings, a cricket pitch and a shelter where old men sit and children kick a ball till dark.

places.name: Ings End Co-operative Store and News Room
places.summary: The branch Co-op with a grocery below and a news room above, where members read the papers for nothing.

places.name: Pickering's pie shop
places.summary: A pie shop with a few tables, selling pork pies, pie and peas with mint sauce, and a jug of gravy for home.

places.name: Ings End Wesleyan Chapel
places.summary: A new stone chapel built by subscription, with a Thursday choir practice and a Band of Hope for the children.

places.name: Head Post Office
places.summary: The post office where the pneumatic post began, with a counter of brass tube mouths and a clerk who sends a letter across town in a minute.

places.name: The Commercial Hotel
places.summary: A hotel for travelling salesmen opposite the station, with sample rooms, a coffee room and a plain table d'hote at six.

places.name: Central Station bookstall
places.summary: A platform bookstall of newspapers, railway novels, timetables and penny maps of the valley.

places.name: Uncle Dick's pawnshop
places.summary: The busiest pawnbroker in town, with Sunday suits going in on Monday and coming out again on Saturday.

places.name: St Patrick's Church
places.summary: The Catholic church at the top of Paradise Street, with early Mass for the works and the Whit procession behind a band.

places.name: The Harp
places.summary: An Irish pub on Paradise Street with a fiddler on Saturday nights and a back room where the Hibernian society meets.

places.name: Ackroyd Park bandstand
places.summary: An iron bandstand by the lake where works brass bands play on Sunday afternoons and the town band on summer evenings.

places.name: Park refreshment pavilion
places.summary: A timber pavilion by the boating lake selling tea, lemonade, buns and ices to families on their Sunday walk.

places.name: Ackroyd Park bowling greens
places.summary: Two corporation greens with a hut for woods, open to anyone with a penny and flat-soled shoes.

places.name: The Shoulder of Mutton
places.summary: A pub on the moor road used by students, porters from the infirmary and art-school teachers arguing about Ruskin.

places.name: St Aidan's, Fernleigh
places.summary: A new stone church paid for by the manufacturers, with carved pews, a good organ and a Sunday parade of hats.

places.name: Fernleigh Hotel dining room
places.summary: A quiet hotel dining room on the omnibus terminus where villa families take Sunday luncheon and wedding breakfasts.

places.name: Fernleigh Subscription Library
places.summary: A subscription library in a converted villa, with new novels from London and a ladies' committee that picks them.

places.name: Ridley Top Farm teas
places.summary: A farmhouse that sells teas, eggs and buttermilk to walkers, with a parlour for wet days and a table outside for fine ones.

places.name: Ridley delph
places.summary: A gritstone quarry on the moor edge where the stone for the town's chapels and villas is cut and dressed in open sheds.

places.name: Holme tea gardens
places.summary: Trestle tables under the alders by the river where families buy a jug of hot water for their own tea and a plate of teacakes.

places.name: The Ferry Boat Inn
places.summary: A riverside pub by the old ferry with a garden of benches, where cyclists stop after the Saturday races.

places.name: Calder Rowing Club
places.summary: A wooden boathouse on the mill dam where clerks and mechanics row fours in the evening and hold a regatta in July.

colleges.name: Royal Infirmary Training School for Nurses

careers.name: Tube fitter
careers.summary: Installing and repairing pneumatic tube runs in shops, banks and offices across town and beyond.

careers.name: Tube drawer
careers.summary: Drawing hot and cold metal tube on the benches of a tube mill, on day and night turns.

careers.name: Boilermaker
careers.summary: Riveting and caulking boiler plate for engines and compressors.

careers.name: Iron moulder
careers.summary: Making sand moulds and pouring castings in a foundry.

careers.name: Draughtsman
careers.summary: Drawing engineering plans in a works drawing office, with evening classes at the Institute.

careers.name: Mill hand
careers.summary: Minding looms in a worsted shed from six in the morning, as many young women in town do.

careers.name: Canal boatman
careers.summary: Working a horse-drawn narrowboat between the basin and the coast with family aboard.

careers.name: Lock-keeper
careers.summary: Keeping a canal lock and its cottage, working the gates for every boat.

careers.name: Railway signalman
careers.summary: Working the levers and bells in a signal box on eight-hour turns.

careers.name: Telegraphist
careers.summary: Sending and taking telegrams at the post office instrument room.

careers.name: Tube post sorter
careers.summary: Sorting and dispatching carriers in the town's pneumatic post office.

careers.name: Airship mail rigger
careers.summary: Handling lines, gas bags and mail at the mooring mast and flying as crew on the mail run.

careers.name: Typist
careers.summary: Typing letters and invoices in a works or merchant's office, one of the new jobs open to young women.

careers.name: Clerk
careers.summary: Keeping ledgers and copying letters in a counting house or company office.

careers.name: Shop assistant
careers.summary: Serving behind the counter in a store, long hours, living in above the shop.

careers.name: Infirmary nurse
careers.summary: Ward nursing at the Royal Infirmary, living in the nurses' home.

careers.name: Board school teacher
careers.summary: Teaching a class of sixty in a board school, mostly children of mill and works families.

careers.name: Institute lecturer
careers.summary: Teaching mechanics and drawing at the Pennock Institute, many classes in the evening.

careers.name: Music hall singer
careers.summary: Singing comic and sentimental songs twice nightly, touring the halls between bookings.

careers.name: Union organiser
careers.summary: Recruiting members and fighting grievances for the tube workers' union.

careers.name: Pastry cook
careers.summary: Baking tarts, pies and cakes from four in the morning for a confectioner and tea room.

careers.name: Compositor
careers.summary: Setting type by hand for the morning paper, through the night.

careers.name: Reporter
careers.summary: Covering council meetings, police court, accidents and football for the town paper.

careers.name: Photographer
careers.summary: Taking studio portraits, wedding groups and works outings.

careers.name: Bar staff
careers.summary: Pulling pints and keeping order in a brewery tied house.

employers.name: Haworth and Pyne Pneumatic Works
employers.summary: The largest firm in town, making and fitting pneumatic dispatch systems for shops, banks and post offices across the country.

employers.name: Ingleby's Drawn Tube Mill
employers.summary: A hot and noisy mill drawing copper and steel tube by the mile, worked round the clock.

employers.name: Dunmore Brothers Engine and Pump Works
employers.summary: Builds the compressors and pumping engines that drive the tube systems, with its own boiler shop and foundry.

employers.name: Sugden and Sons Worsted Mill
employers.summary: The old family mill on the river, still spinning and weaving worsted with a mostly female workforce.

employers.name: Calder and Aske Navigation Company
employers.summary: Owns the canal, the basin, the warehouses and the lock cottages, and hires out boats.

employers.name: Calder Valley Railway
employers.summary: Runs Central station, the goods yards and the valley line.

employers.name: Calderwick Corporation Gasworks
employers.summary: The municipal gasworks by the basin, lighting the streets and supplying the tube post engines.

employers.name: Calderwick Royal Infirmary
employers.summary: The town hospital, paid for by subscription and works collections, busy with works accidents.

employers.name: The Calderwick Examiner
employers.summary: The daily paper, Liberal in politics, printed overnight behind its Exchange Street office.

employers.name: Pennock Institute
employers.summary: The engineering institute founded by a pump maker, teaching day and evening classes.

employers.name: Calderwick Pneumatic and Telegraph Office
employers.summary: The post office instrument room and the hub of the town's pneumatic post.

employers.name: Ridley Moor Air Mail Company
employers.summary: Runs the single mail airship and its mast crew.

employers.name: Wright and Battersby
employers.summary: The department store, with live-in assistants and a counting house fed by cash tubes.

employers.name: Whiteley's Confectioners
employers.summary: A confectioner and tea room baking for weddings, funerals and Saturday afternoons.

employers.name: Calderwick School Board
employers.summary: Runs the board schools in the terraces and Paradise.

employers.name: Amalgamated Society of Tube Workers
employers.summary: The union of tube drawers and fitters, meeting upstairs at Hope Street.

employers.name: Thornber's Varieties
employers.summary: The music hall and its company of turns.

employers.name: Ackworth's Calder Brewery
employers.summary: The local brewery and its tied pubs across the valley.

employers.name: Fothergill's Photographic Studio
employers.summary: A portrait studio with a glass roof and painted backdrops.

career_hubs.name: Lowfield works
career_hubs.summary: The tube mills, pump works, foundries and the worsted shed along the river.

career_hubs.name: Exchange Quarter offices and shops
career_hubs.summary: Banks, merchants' counting houses, the newspaper, the post office and the shops.

career_hubs.name: Basin and railway
career_hubs.summary: The canal basin, gasworks, station yards, music hall and the airship mast.

career_hubs.name: Moorside institutions
career_hubs.summary: The Infirmary, the Pennock Institute and the art school.

climate.summary: Cool and wet Pennine weather: mild summers, long grey winters, rain in every month and smoke fogs in the valley bottom on still winter days.

months.note: Raw and dark; smoke fogs sit in Lowfield for days.
Cold, with sleet and snow on the moor.
Wind and showers; the first light evenings.
Bright spells, curlews back on the moor.
Long light evenings and the smoke lifts.
Warmest month; the lido opens fully.
Wet and windy; fires lit again.
Dark by half past four; fog returns.
Cold and grey; the worst smog of the year.

annual_events.name: Mast Day
annual_events.summary: Crowds walk up the moor to see the mail airship come back from her winter overhaul and take the first bags of the year.

annual_events.name: Whit Walks
annual_events.summary: Sunday schools and chapels march through town behind banners and bands, children in new clothes, then tea and races in the park.

annual_events.name: Saltergate canal regatta
annual_events.summary: Rowing, sculling and decorated-boat races on the basin, with a greasy pole and a boatmen's tug of war.

annual_events.name: Infirmary Sunday gala
annual_events.summary: Band concerts and a procession in Ackroyd Park collecting for the Royal Infirmary.

annual_events.name: Pennock Institute exhibition
annual_events.summary: Students show engines, models and drawings, and the firms come looking for apprentices.

annual_events.name: Calder Wakes Week
annual_events.summary: The works and mills shut for a week; the town empties to the seaside and those who stay crowd the lido and the pier.

annual_events.name: Valley cycling championship
annual_events.summary: The big race meeting of the season at the velodrome, with bookmakers under the stand and a band between heats.

annual_events.name: Calderwick Charter Fair
annual_events.summary: The old market charter fair: steam roundabouts, coconut shies, brandy snap stalls and a hiring of farm servants on the first day.

annual_events.name: Bonfire Night
annual_events.summary: Every street in the terraces builds a bonfire on the fifth, with parkin, toffee and treacle.

annual_events.name: Lantern procession
annual_events.summary: Children and choirs carry paper lanterns up Kirkgate to the castle on the shortest day, ending with carols at St Wilfrid's.

annual_events.name: Pantomime season
annual_events.summary: The Theatre Royal pantomime runs from Boxing Day, with works outings booking whole rows.

local_color.name: Parkin
local_color.summary: A dark, sticky oatmeal and treacle gingerbread, baked in slabs for Bonfire Night and better a week after.

local_color.name: Chumping
local_color.summary: In the weeks before Bonfire Night children go "chumping", collecting wood for their street's bonfire and guarding the pile from rival streets.

local_color.name: Yorkshire pudding first
local_color.summary: The batter pudding comes to the table on its own with gravy before the meat, so that a family fills up before the joint is cut.

local_color.name: Pie and peas
local_color.summary: A hot pork or meat-and-potato pie with mushy peas and mint sauce, the supper of the works and the market.

local_color.name: Tripe and onions
local_color.summary: Tripe stewed in milk with onions, or eaten cold with salt and vinegar, from the tripe dresser's.

local_color.name: Oatcake on the creel
local_color.summary: Soft oatcakes are hung to dry on a wooden rack over the range and eaten fresh and floppy, or crisp and toasted with dripping.

local_color.name: Forced rhubarb
local_color.summary: Rhubarb grown in the dark in forcing sheds comes pink and tender in the cold months, stewed with custard or baked in a pie.

local_color.name: A pint of mild
local_color.summary: Dark, sweetish mild ale is the working man's pint, drunk in quantity after a shift at the tube mill or the foundry.

local_color.name: Dandelion and burdock
local_color.summary: Chapel folk and the temperance halls drink dandelion and burdock, sarsaparilla and ginger beer instead of ale.

local_color.name: "Nowt", "owt" and "summat"
local_color.summary: Nothing, anything and something: "Has tha got owt?" "Nowt." Older people still say "thee" and "tha" to family and friends.

local_color.name: Ginnel
local_color.summary: A narrow passage between houses or through to the back street; Calderwick uses "ginnel", and a stranger from the next valley may say "snicket".

local_color.name: "Ey up"
local_color.summary: The everyday greeting, meaning hello or look out, usually followed by "love" or "lad" whoever you are.

local_color.name: "Where there's muck there's brass"
local_color.summary: Where there is dirt there is money: the town's answer to anyone who complains about the smoke from the tube mills.

local_color.name: "Mash the tea"
local_color.summary: Tea is "mashed" rather than brewed, strong, in a brown pot, and offered to anyone who comes to the door.

local_color.name: "Tube it"
local_color.summary: To send a note across town by the pneumatic post; a quick answer is "back down the tube", and a lost one "gone up the pipe".

local_color.name: The knocker-up
local_color.summary: Before the six o'clock hooter a knocker-up goes along the terraces tapping on bedroom windows with a long pole, paid a few pence a week by each house.

local_color.name: Donkey-stoning the step
local_color.summary: Women scour their front doorsteps and window sills with a donkey stone, a cream or white scouring block, and judge a street by its steps.

local_color.name: The Co-op divi
local_color.summary: Every member's purchases earn a share of the profits, the "divi", paid out twice a year; families quote their check number like a name.

local_color.name: Popping it at Uncle's
local_color.summary: Pawning, usually the Sunday suit on a Monday to be redeemed on Saturday payday; "Uncle's" is the pawnbroker.

local_color.name: The clogger
local_color.summary: Most of the town walks on clogs, and the clogger cuts alder soles, fits the uppers and nails on fresh irons while you sit in your stockings.
